_why: The numbering epoch: which slug each section number names, and the roadmap of record that numbers them. Section numbers are a property of the epoch, not of the section, so no fixer tool may type a section count; tools/fixer/numbering.py reads everything from this file and checks it against the roadmap, the course order and each section file index.
_contract: numbering_epoch is the count of sections in the table, and it names the epoch: state that carries another label belongs to another numbering and is refused. A renumber does not edit this file by hand: after the renumber changes the course and the roadmap, `python3 tools/fixer/restamp.py advance --roadmap <the new roadmap>` writes the next epoch from the course, moves this table into previous_epochs, and re-keys the cycle records, the redaction list and the finding registry by slug. previous_epochs is how that carry knows what each old number named; it is never deleted.
_relation: Not the same file as audit/safe-agent/renumber_epoch.json. This one is the fixer's table: which slug each number names now, for the life of the course. renumber_epoch.json (the preservation guards G-11 and G-15, schema renumber_epoch/1) is the renumber window's switch: the renumber commit writes it, it names the commit and the sections that commit added, and its presence arms those guards. The window closes and the table does not, so they are kept apart. When renumber_epoch.json exists, `new_slugs` must be exactly the (slug, number) pairs this table has and the latest previous_epochs table did not; numbering.check_epoch checks it.
